transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

Hi. Yeah, um, well... what finally scared me into coming in is that I just keep making these really dumb technical mistakes at work. And I know better! I'm an editor and a camera operator, so I've been doing this a long time. Actually, I just got off this massive reality TV shoot last week—we were out in the middle of nowhere for like four days, and the catering was just awful. Honestly, it was just stale bagels and lukewarm coffee, which I really can't stand because I need my coffee piping hot, you know? My sister used to work at a coffee shop and she always told me the secret to a good brew is... wait, what was I saying? 

Oh, right, why I'm here. Yeah, so I'm doing things like labeling camera cards wrong, or completely missing a timecode note. The worst is when I export a client cut with the wrong lower-third graphic on the screen... and that's even after I’ve checked it! It's just getting really embarrassing and I'm scared it's going to cost me my job.
When you were a child, did you often have trouble paying attention or staying organized?

Oh, yeah, absolutely. It's funny you ask about childhood because my mom just found this huge box of my old report cards when she was cleaning out the garage. She’s trying to downsize, you know? She wants to move to this condo near the beach, which is great, but the HOA fees are just insane. I told her she should look a little further inland, but she loves the ocean. Anyway, those report cards... yeah, it was always the same thing. Even in elementary school, they were always moving my desk right up next to the teacher's. I was just constantly out of my seat, or I'd just blurt out the answers before anyone else could, or I'd be poking or talking to whoever was sitting next to me. Half the time I didn't even realize I was doing it until the teacher yelled at me.
Have these focus and organization problems been present pretty much your whole adult life?

Well, um... not my whole adult life, no. I mean, I've always been a little scattered, but it really hasn't been this bad until, gosh, about two years and two months ago? Yeah, that sounds right. That's when my company went through this massive readjustment. They totally changed how our shoots are scheduled and how the edit reviews run. It used to be this really collaborative thing where we'd all sit in the editing bay, and my old producer, Dave—oh my gosh, Dave was the best. He had this vintage popcorn machine in his office, like an actual movie theater one, and he'd make popcorn for every single review session. The whole hallway smelled like butter on Thursdays. He retired to Maine, actually. Bought a boat, which I am so jealous of. I’ve always wanted to learn how to sail, but the knots seem really complicated. 

But yeah, since the readjustment, everything is just... different. It's been going on at this super disruptive level ever since they changed the workflow. I just can't seem to keep up with the new system.
About when this got markedly worse two years ago, did it start after a head injury?

A head injury? No, no, definitely not. I haven't hit my head or anything like that. I did fall off my bike once when I was a kid, scraped my knee pretty bad, but no head stuff. Actually, I was riding my bike just the other day—I have one of those vintage cruisers, you know, with the wide handlebars and the big basket on the front? I found it at this flea market downtown. The guy selling it was this amazing local artist who makes sculptures out of old bicycle chains. I ended up buying one of his little dog sculptures for my desk, it's so cute. But yeah, I was riding down by the river and it was just gorgeous out, though the gnats were terrible. I probably swallowed like three of them. 

Wait, what were we talking about? Oh, right, head injury. No, nothing like that. Just the workflow changes at work, really.
Around the time your focus got much worse, were you feeling depressed most days?

Depressed? Um, no, not really. I mean, I was stressed, sure, because of all the new scheduling stuff, but not depressed. Actually, it's funny you mention feeling down, because right around that time, my sister adopted this rescue dog, a Greyhound. They are so weirdly skinny, you know? Like, you can see all their ribs, and you feel like you need to feed them a cheeseburger, but apparently, that's just how they're supposed to look. She named him Barnaby. He's super sweet, but he has this thing where he just freezes on walks. Like, completely statuesque. She had to carry him home once, and he's like sixty pounds of just elbows and knees. It was hilarious, but also her back was killing her for a week. She ended up having to go to this chiropractor who uses, like, lasers? I don't know, it sounded very sci-fi to me. I told her just to get a heating pad, but she loves all that alternative stuff. 

But anyway, depressed? No. Just really, really overwhelmed with the new edit bays and trying to keep everything straight.
Have you ever had a period where you felt unusually energetic or wired for several days in a row?

Unusually energetic? Like, wired? Um... no, I don't think so. I mean, I have energy, obviously, because I'm always moving around, but not like... not like a whole period of days where I'm just buzzing. I did drink way too much espresso once, though. Have you ever been to that little coffee shop on 4th Street? The one with the exposed brick and the baristas who look like they're in a band? They make this drink called the "Red Eye Flight" and it's basically just shots of espresso poured over more espresso. I had one before a massive edit session because I thought it would help me focus on the new system, but instead, I just ended up reorganizing all the cables behind my monitors for three hours. Color-coded them and everything. I even used those little velcro ties. They're amazing, honestly. I bought a pack of like a hundred on Amazon for five bucks. You can use them for everything—I even used one to tie up my tomato plants on my balcony. Tomatoes are so hard to grow, though, right? The birds keep getting to mine before they even turn red. My neighbor put up a plastic owl to scare them away, but I swear the pigeons just sit on its head now. 

But yeah, no, not like a whole period of being wired for days. Just the normal amount of energy, I guess. Well, normal for me.
Do you tend to worry excessively about lots of different things, even when there isn’t an immediate problem?

Worry excessively? I mean, not really. I'm not a big worrier. I just get frustrated when I can't get things done. But worry... no. My mom is a huge worrier, though. Oh my gosh, she worries about everything. She called me the other day in an absolute panic because she read this article online about how the blue light from screens is destroying our retinas. And I'm an editor, so I'm staring at screens literally all day. She wanted me to buy these special glasses, they're like... yellow tinted? They look terrible. I tried a pair on at the pharmacy once, just for fun, and they made me look like I was in a 70s disco movie. Speaking of 70s movies, did you ever see Saturday Night Fever? The soundtrack is just incredible. I actually have it on vinyl. I started collecting vinyl a few years ago. There's just something about the sound, you know? It's warmer. I found this amazing vintage record player at a garage sale, but the needle was broken, so I had to order a replacement part from Germany. It took like a month to get here, and the instructions were all in German, so I had to use Google Translate on my phone to figure out how to install it. It was a whole project. 

Wait, what did you ask me? Something about worrying? Yeah, no, I don't really worry about stuff like that. Just my mom.
